title: One smooth hypersurface slice at a separable closed fibre point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $x\in X$ map to $s\in S$, with $x$ closed in the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Assume that $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is finite (finite-dimensional as a vector space) and separable algebraic [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and that $\dim_x(X_s)=d$ for an integer $d\geq1$, with dimension at a point as in [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Then there exist an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $x$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and an effective Cartier divisor $D\hookrightarrow U$ [def-trf-effective-cartier-center, def-weil-closed-immersion] containing $x$, such that the composite $D\to U\to X\to S$ is smooth and $\dim_x(D_s)=d-1$. Here $x$ in $D$ denotes the unique point mapping to the specified $x\in U$.

source.place: Tag 057F, lemma-slice-smooth-once-separable-residue-field-extension, specialized to a closed fibre point of positive dimension; Tag 057C, lemma-slice-smooth-given-element, proof, displayed dimension drop for the chosen hypersurface.

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(s)$ and $L=\kappa(x)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension], choose affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq S$ about $x,s$, with $f(W)\subseteq V$, such that $\Omega_{A/B}$ is free of rank $d$. The map $W\to S$ is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. It is smooth as a map to $V$ as well: local finite presentation uses the same target affine neighbourhoods, and a lifting square over $V$ is a lifting square over $S$, whose lift is still over $V$ because $V\to S$ is a monomorphism. Now [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] makes $B\to A$ smooth. In particular $A$ is finitely presented over $B$. Set $C=k\otimes_B A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], $W_s=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is the open of $X_s$ above $W$. Let $\mathfrak q$ be its point corresponding to $x$, and put $R=C_{\mathfrak q}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak qR$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $R=\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$. Its residue field is $L$: [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] identifies $R$ with $\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_s\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and this ideal is inside $\mathfrak m_x$, so passage to the residue field gives $\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x$. The algebra $C$ is finite type over $k$, since the images of any finite algebra-generating set of $A/B$ generate $C/k$.

source.place: Tags 057C and 057D, affine/fibre local-ring setup; Morphisms Tags 02G1 and 01UT; Schemes Tag 0HA1

proof.text:
Let $E=\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R L$. Differential base change [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] gives $\Omega_{C/k}\cong C\otimes_A\Omega_{A/B}$, and differential localization [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] then gives
$$E\cong\Omega_{C/k}\otimes_C L\cong\Omega_{A/B}\otimes_A L\cong L^d.$$
For the first identification $(\omega/t)\otimes\lambda$ maps to $\omega\otimes\bar t^{-1}\lambda$, with inverse $\omega\otimes\lambda\mapsto(\omega/1)\otimes\lambda$; the middle identification cancels the $C$ tensor factor by $(c\otimes\omega)\otimes\lambda\mapsto\omega\otimes\bar c\lambda$. The last identification tensors the basis from step 1. Thus $E\ne0$, since $d\geq1$ and $L$ is a field. Moreover these identifications carry differentials to differentials. By [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization], they also identify $E$ with $\Omega^1_{X/S,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}L$, carrying the relative differential of a germ to the differential of its fibre image.

source.place: Tag 057D, identification of fibre differentials; Algebra Tags 00RV and 00RT; Morphisms Tag 01UT

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] to $k\to R\to L=R/\mathfrak m$. It gives an exact sequence
$$\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\xrightarrow{\delta}E\longrightarrow\Omega_{L/k}\longrightarrow0,\qquad \delta(\bar h\bmod\mathfrak m^2)=d\bar h\otimes1.$$
The extension $L/k$ is finite separable by hypothesis, so $\Omega_{L/k}=0$ by [lem-trf-separable-field-differentials-vanish]. Hence $\delta$ is surjective. Choose a nonzero vector of $E$ and a preimage under $\delta$, represented by $\bar h\in\mathfrak m$. Then $d\bar h\otimes1\ne0$. By the surjection of [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient], lift $\bar h$ to $h\in\mathcal O_{X,x}$. The quotient has maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_s\mathcal O_{X,x}$, so $h\in\mathfrak m_x$. Step 2 identifies $dh\otimes1$ with the chosen nonzero vector. This is the needed local equation, obtained from the full conormal exact sequence rather than merely from vanishing of $\Omega_{L/k}$.

source.place: Tag 057D, exact conormal sequence and lifting of the germ; Tag 057G, positive-dimensional case using finite-separable differential vanishing; Algebra Tags 00RU and 090W

proof.text:
By smooth base change [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](1), $C$ is smooth over $k$. Thus $R=C_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local], and is an integral domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. Since $d ar h\otimes1
e0$, we have $ ar h
e0$; multiplication by $ ar h$ on $R$ is injective. Use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] on $W$ to write $h=b/t$ with $b,t\in A$ and $t(x)
e0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], $U_0=D_W(t)$ is affine and $a=b/t\in\Gamma(U_0,\mathcal O)$ has germ $h$. Let $Z=V(a)\subseteq U_0$. It contains $x$ because $h\in\mathfrak m_x$. As the zero scheme of the section $a$ of the trivial rank-one module, it is locally principal and closed by [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties]. Its fibre equation has germ $ ar h$ at $x$.

source.place: Tag 057C, the equation is fibre-regular; Algebra Tags 00TT and 00NP; extension of the germ as in Tag 056Y, first paragraph

proof.text: Write $C_0=C[1/\bar t]$, so $(U_0)_s=\operatorname{Spec}C_0$, and let $a_s\in C_0$ be the fibre image of $a$. The affine fibre-product formula of step 1 identifies $Z_s$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(C_0/(a_s))$: the tensor isomorphism sends $\lambda\otimes(c\bmod a)$ to the class of $\lambda\otimes c$, with inverse induced by $\lambda\otimes c\mapsto\lambda\otimes(c\bmod a)$. The ring $C_0$ is finite type over $k$ (adjoin an inverse of $\bar t$), hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field. Let $I=\operatorname{Ann}_{C_0}(a_s)$ and choose finite generators $u_1,\ldots,u_n$. Each $(u_i)_x$ is zero because $a_s$ is a nonzerodivisor in $R$. The localization description [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] supplies $v_i$ outside the prime of $x$ with $v_iu_i=0$. Put $v=\prod_i v_i$ (or $1$ if $n=0$). In $(C_0)_v$ multiplication by $a_s$ is injective: if $a_s c/v^r=0$, some $v^N a_s c=0$, so $v^Nc\in I$, and $vI=0$. Thus $Z_s$ is an effective Cartier divisor near $x$, by the locally-one-nonzerodivisor definition [def-trf-effective-cartier-center].

source.place: Tag 057C and Divisors Tag 062Y, verification of the fibre-Cartier hypothesis; finite-annihilator argument as Algebra Tag 00FN

proof.text: The open restriction $U_0\to S$ is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The closed subscheme $Z\subseteq U_0$ is locally principal, and step 5 proves that $Z_s$ is effective Cartier near $x$. All hypotheses of [lem-pc-recd-fibre-cartier-local] therefore hold. It gives an ambient open neighbourhood $U_1\subseteq U_0$ of $x$ such that $Z\cap U_1$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor. By [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier], it is in particular an effective Cartier divisor on $U_1$.

source.place: Tag 057C, use of the fibre-regular equation to obtain a Cartier cut; Divisors Tag 062Y(3), lemma-fibre-Cartier

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-hypersurface-nonzero-relative-differential] to the smooth morphism $U_0\to S$, the trivial invertible module $\mathcal O_{U_0}$, its section $a$, and $Z=V(a)$. The module is invertible by its single global basis $1$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. Its relative differential at $x$ is the nonzero vector from steps 2--3, since $a_x=h$. The cited lemma gives an open neighbourhood $N$ of $x$ in $Z$ on which $Z\to S$ is smooth. By the subspace topology of the closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], choose an open $O\subseteq U_0$ with $Z\cap O=N$. Inside the open $O\cap U_1$ choose a principal open $U=D_{U_0}(g)$ containing $x$, using [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]; it is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]. Set $D=Z\cap U$. The Cartier property on $U_1$ restricts to $U$: the same local nonzerodivisor generators work on smaller opens [def-trf-effective-cartier-center]. The morphism $D\to S$ is smooth because $D$ is an open subscheme of $N$, by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. Its closed immersion into $U$ is the principal quotient construction, and it contains $x$.

source.place: Tag 057C, nonzero-differential smoothness and final shrinking; the existing nonzero-relative-differential hypersurface criterion, with its explicit standard smooth proof

proof.text:
It remains to compute the dimension of this particular cut. The affine fibre description in step 5 and the final principal localization give
$$\mathcal O_{D_s,x}\cong R/(\bar h).$$
Indeed localizing $C_0/(a_s)$ at the point of $x$ sends $(c\bmod a_s)/(u\bmod a_s)$ to the class of $c/u$ in $R/(\bar h)$; lifting numerator and denominator defines the inverse. Further restriction to the open $U$ changes neither local ring. The ring $R$ is Noetherian local, and $\bar h\in\mathfrak m$ is a nonzerodivisor by steps 3--4. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] gives $\dim(R/(\bar h))+1=\dim R$. Its residue field is still $L$, since $(R/(\bar h))/(\mathfrak m/(\bar h))=R/\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-kun-dimension-formula] to the finite-type $k$-schemes $(U_0)_s=\operatorname{Spec}C_0$ and $Z_s=\operatorname{Spec}(C_0/(a_s))$. The extension $L/k$ is finite algebraic, so its transcendence degree is zero: an algebraically independent nonempty set would contain a transcendental element. Thus their dimensions at $x$ are respectively $\dim R$ and $\dim(R/(\bar h))$. The open-fibre identification [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] identify these with $\dim_x(X_s)=d$ and $\dim_x(D_s)$. Consequently $\dim_x(D_s)+1=d$, hence $\dim_x(D_s)=d-1$. The point in $D$ above $x$ is unique because a closed immersion is injective on underlying points [def-weil-closed-immersion].
